title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.64
statement: Let $\alpha$ be real and suppose that $f(z)=z+\sum^\infty_{n=2}a_nz^n$ is analytic in $\mathbb{D}$ with $f(z)f'(z)/z\neq0$. We say $f$ is in $M_\alpha$, the class of alpha-convex functions, if \[\text{Re}\,\Big[(1-\alpha)\frac{zf'}{f}+\alpha\Big(1+\frac{zf''}{f'}\Big)\Big]>0\] for $|z|<1$. Note that $M_0=S^*$, the class of star-like functions and $M_1=K$, the class of convex functions. It is known that $M_\alpha\subset S^*$ for all $\alpha$. Clunie and Keogh have shown the following: [(a)] ; If $\sum^\infty_{n=2}n|a_n|<1$ then $f\in M_0$ ; If $\sum^\infty_{n=2}n^2|a_n|<1$ then $f\in M_1$. What generalisation of these conditions implies that $f$ belongs to $M_\alpha$? (S. Miller)
